text:
Kai Chen: noticed a regression in KV reuse across requests after the long-context rollout. hit rate for prefix cache dropped ~18% on canary, memory growth steady for sessions >30k tokens
Maria Gomez: ugh, saw that too. full profilings? logs?
Kai Chen: stacktrace not relevant, ran perf traces + heap snapshots. kv pages increasing, lots of small tombstones, fragmentation seems high. attaching quick numbers: kv_pages: +24% over baseline, avg_page_free_fragment: 18%
Samir Patel: do we have which keys are dominating? tenant vs model vs prefix?
Kai Chen: most churn under same tenant/model but different prompt prefixes. our current key = sha256(tenant + model + prompt_prefix) so small changes in prefix explode key cardinality
Maria Gomez: that matches suspicion — prefix entropy. We probably need a lower-entropy fingerprint for prefix portion. e.g. deterministic prefix fingerprint up to N tokens
Lucy Nguyen: also saw eviction storms where a single longctx session pins many pages. eviction sweeps then evict unrelated small hot prefixes -> thrash
Samir Patel: could we try partitioned sticky buckets? keep a session-local bucket that keeps recent prefix fingerprints sticky, but limit bucket size and age
Kai Chen: idea sketch: global LRU for shared prefixes + session-local mini-slab where we write most-recent prefixes for that session. on session end or TTL they demote back to global. reduces cross-session fragmentation
Maria Gomez: also consider compacting key shape: instead of full prefix hash, store (prefix_fingerprint_64, prefix_len_bucket, tenant_id, model_id). reduces uniqueness for near-identical prefixes
Samir Patel: we must be careful with collisions — 64-bit ok if we accept rare false positives, faster reuse. Need tests for correctness regression though
Lucy Nguyen: operationally: collect heatmap of prefix_fingerprint -> residency time, miss-after-hit rate, and slab fragmentation per node. We need instrumentation first
ops-bot: new run created: kv-prefp-instrumentation-6598765432 (job id: job-9271) :white_check_mark:
Kai Chen: thanks. next steps I propose:
- add instrumentation (prefix_fingerprint, residency_ms, evicted_by) to KV metrics
- prototype session-local bucket in runtime (config flag) with small default size 64 entries
- run canary with compact key shape and session bucket on 10% traffic
Maria Gomez: +1. I'll own the instrumentation PR. will include heatmap endpoint and per-tenant breakdown
Samir Patel: I'll implement a prototype of session bucket and a compact key serializer. rough plan: two new runtime knobs: session_bucket_size, prefix_fingerprint_bits
Lucy Nguyen: I'll prepare perf test harness (longctx replay) to repro mem growth: three scenarios - baseline, compact-key-only, compact-key+session-bucket
Kai Chen: quick pseudo for key calc (will refine):
```
// key = tenant: model : fingerprint64 : len_bucket
fingerprint64 = xxhash64(prefix_normalized)
len_bucket = min(prefix_token_count / 8, 7)
```
Samir Patel: looks good. normalization: strip punctuation, lowercase, truncate repeating tokens
Maria Gomez: also instrument eviction cause: is_evicted_for_ttl | evicted_for_mem_pressure | evicted_due_to_collision. we need to see which ones correlate with thrash
Lucy Nguyen: one more thought — slab allocator for per-node KV pages by page size class. fragmentation currently from many small allocations in large pages. moving to size classes could reduce internal fragmentation
Kai Chen: good point. slab change is heavier but maybe high ROI. milestone: do instrumentation first, then session-bucket prototype, run canary, then slab exploration if still bad
Samir Patel: agree. timeline: inst PR by EOD Friday, session-bucket prototype early next week, canary mid next week
Maria Gomez: will also add alert for sudden drop in prefix_hit_rate (>10% drop sustained 5m) and mem_growth_per_session > 1GB/hour for sessions > 20k tokens
Lucy Nguyen: logging note: avoid logging full prefixes. only store fingerprints and lengths for privacy
Kai Chen: volunteers: Maria (metrics + alerts), Samir (session-bucket + compact keys), Lucy (perf harness + heatmaps). I'll run the canary and validate correctness/regressions
ops-bot: deploy pipeline triggered: build-3221 -> canary cluster (tag: kv-reuse-experiments)
Samir Patel: one caveat: compacting keys increases collision risk for prefix-aware rerankers. we'll need to ensure downstream model priming logic tolerates a reuse collision
Maria Gomez: add test: for a sample of collisions, confirm token-level outputs are stable or fallback to re-compute if mismatch
Kai Chen: ok capturing action items in GH issue and will assign. thanks all :thumbsup:
